title: Float-test eggs: lower each into a bowl of water without cracking it, then lift the floating one out into a dish
instruction: Lower each egg into the bowl of water without cracking it, then lift any egg that floats out into the small dish and leave the others in the bowl.
context: The float test is the kitchen check many people learn for eggs of unknown age: in a bowl of cold water a fresh egg sinks and lies on its side, an older one sinks and stands on end, and a very old one floats and is set aside (USU Extension; Egg Safety Center). The hard part is the handling. An egg can crack if it is squeezed hard or let fall onto glass from about a centimeter, so each egg must be picked up with a light grip and let go only at the water's surface. The floater then has to be picked out of the water: a wet, smooth egg standing upright, with only a few millimeters showing, held lightly enough not to crack it and firmly enough not to slip, and set down in the dish. In the sim the eggs look alike, so the robot finds out which one floats only once it is in the water; the score needs all three tested in the water first.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases, on the table top (x forward, y left). Bowl: clear glass 2.5 qt mixing bowl (Anchor Hocking 81575L20: top 8 5/8 in, bottom 4 5/8 in, 4 1/4 in high), centered at x 32, y 0, holding 1.2 L of cold tap water (7.5 cm deep), on a thin non-slip silicone mat. Eggs: three brown eggs lying on their sides on a red cotton tea towel folded to 13 x 22 cm (centered at x 30, y 23), long axes along x, their middles at y 16, 23 and 30. Two sink and one floats (blunt end up, about 5 mm showing in the sim); which place holds the floater is shuffled per trial. Sim: US Large eggs, 56.7 mm long x 42.1 mm across: a fresh egg (57.0 g, lies on its side), an older egg (53.9 g, stands on end) and a floater (51.1 g). Real trial: three US Large brown eggs from one new carton: two fresh (both sink and lie on their side) and one emptied through a hole at each end and refilled with about 4 g of plasticine (Crayola Modeling Clay) at its narrow tip and cold tap water to 0.9 times the whole egg's weight (51 g for a 57 g egg), so that it floats blunt end up; its holes are sealed with plasticine and tape, and the operator knows it by them. Discard dish: clear glass 8.5 oz ramekin (Duralex Ovenchef: top 3 7/8 in, 2 in high), empty, at x 30, y -20.5, on the mat. Nothing else on the table; arms in the ready pose.
scoring: 0 if at any time an egg that is not held (both fingertips of one hand pressing it from opposite sides) moves faster than 0.40 m/s in any direction, or an egg, held or not, first touches the glass, table, towel or another egg faster than that, or while touching one has its velocity change by more than that in one physics step: the speed of a free fall of 8 mm (real trial: video shows it let go more than 8 mm above the water, the glass or the table, thrown, or knocked or rammed into something); or an egg is pressed harder than 38 N in 3 of any 4 physics steps (1/80 s) or 76 N in one (1/240 s), by any one robot link, either arm's links together, both arms' links together, or everything else together (glass, table, towel, the other eggs) (real trial: these limits are scored in the sim only; all three eggs, the floater included, are real eggshells, so squeezing or knocking any egg harder than its shell takes cracks it, and an egg with a crack, seen by eye or by candling it with a phone flashlight after the trial, scores 0); or an egg leaves the table; or (real trial) the bowl is knocked off its mat or water spills over its rim. Otherwise 0 until every egg has been tested: each has sat in the bowl's water, not touched by the robot, for 1 s. 0.25 once all three have been tested; 0.5 and the floater out of the bowl, with the other two lying or standing on the bowl's floor (lowest point within 1.2 cm of it) and not touched; 0.75 and the floater on the ramekin's floor (lowest point within 1.2 cm of it, its middle inside the ramekin) and not touched; 1.0 and every egg at rest (under 1 cm/s) with every link of both arms 2 cm or more from every egg, held 1 s. A good egg taken out of the bowl, or the floater left in it, stays at 0.25. Doing nothing scores 0. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0.
reset_notes: Lift the three eggs out; candle each against a phone flashlight in a dim room before drying it (a crack scores 0 and that egg is replaced); dry them and lay them back on the towel at their marks; top the bowl up to 1.2 L of cold water. Candle every egg before its first trial too. Sinkers: two fresh eggs from a new carton, refrigerated between sessions. Floater: made once and reused until its shell cracks; make three at once from the carton (two spares). For each: weigh the whole egg; target = 0.9 x that (57 g -> 51 g); prick a hole in each end with a thumbtack, open the blunt-end one to about 5 mm with a small Phillips screwdriver; blow the contents out through the narrow-end hole, rinse, dry overnight; seal the narrow-end hole with plasticine and tape; push in about 4 g of plasticine (Crayola Modeling Clay) in small pieces and press it into the narrow tip; in a ramekin on a zeroed kitchen scale, add cold tap water with a 10 mL oral syringe to 1 g under the target (about 40 mL for a 57 g egg); seal the hole with plasticine and tape; it floats blunt end up, tip clearly above the water. Before each session (1 minute): weigh the floater (1 g under its target to its target; lighter: top up; heavier: use a spare); float the three: both fresh eggs sink, the floater floats blunt end up with its tip clearly above the water. Robot: cover each finger with a nitrile glove finger or thin silicone sleeve (README); stop the trial if water reaches the gripper body.
fidelity: No fluid is simulated: a force model adds buoyancy (from the bowl's water level) and quadratic drag (Cd 0.5); no waves, slosh or surface tension. Each egg is a rigid egg-curve hull, its mass and center of mass set by its air cell. Cracks are judged from speed and force. Real trial: both sinkers are fresh (the sim's older sinker stands); the refilled floater matches the sim's in size, mass and float height; its contents are water with a free air bubble, kept blunt end up by plasticine at its tip.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0; demo: 1.0 in 3 of 3 runs (scripted, fixed plan, EGG_SEED=0)
